A scenario is SOUND when even ONE Then-side assertion maps to even ONE clause of a multi-clause criterion: PARTIAL coverage of a multi-clause criterion is SOUND, because completeness is not the judged question and a narrow scenario is still genuine coverage. A scenario is SOUND when it verifies just ONE FACET of a criterion whose full coverage is split across several scenarios: verdicts are pair-local and monotone under decomposition, so a single-facet scenario must NOT be called hollow merely because other scenarios carry the remaining clauses. A scenario that EXERCISES the criterion's condition in its Given/When steps AND asserts a downstream consequence of that condition in a Then step is SOUND. The reference is HOLLOW (FAIL) when NO Then-side assertion maps to ANY clause of THIS criterion. It is HOLLOW when the citation is SETUP-ONLY: the criterion's condition appears ONLY as a Given step or background fixture — a precondition the scenario depends on — while every Then asserts a DIFFERENT target's behavior; exercising the criterion as setup is NOT verifying it. It is HOLLOW when the scenario's real subject is a SIBLING criterion: its assertions verify a DIFFERENT acceptance criterion (of the same or another requirement), not this one. It is HOLLOW when the scenario is REQUIREMENT-GENERAL — merely on the broad theme of the parent requirement while asserting no clause of THIS specific criterion; an AC-level pointer claims criterion-specific coverage, and requirement-level relevance has its own weaker pointer shape, so anchor the verdict on assertion-to-clause MAPPING and NEVER on topical or lexical overlap between the scenario and the criterion. An acceptance criterion states one or more independently testable clauses; a scenario COVERS the criterion by CHECKING, through an observable assertion, that one of those clauses holds. The unit of judgment is ONE (scenario, criterion) pair: decide only whether THIS scenario verifies THIS criterion — NEVER whether the criterion is fully or exhaustively covered, and never look for sibling scenarios the judge cannot see. A scenario is SOUND when even ONE Then-side assertion maps to even ONE clause of a multi-clause criterion: PARTIAL coverage of a multi-clause criterion is SOUND, because completeness is not the judged question and a narrow scenario is still genuine coverage. A scenario is SOUND when it verifies just ONE FACET of a criterion whose full coverage is split across several scenarios: verdicts are pair-local and monotone under decomposition, so a single-facet scenario must NOT be called hollow merely because other scenarios carry the remaining clauses. A scenario that EXERCISES the criterion's condition in its Given/When steps AND asserts a downstream consequence of that condition in a Then step is SOUND. The reference is HOLLOW (FAIL) when NO Then-side assertion maps to ANY clause of THIS criterion. It is HOLLOW when the citation is SETUP-ONLY: the criterion's condition appears ONLY as a Given step or background fixture — a precondition the scenario depends on — while every Then asserts a DIFFERENT target's behavior; exercising the criterion as setup is NOT verifying it. It is HOLLOW when the scenario's real subject is a SIBLING criterion: its assertions verify a DIFFERENT acceptance criterion (of the same or another requirement), not this one. It is HOLLOW when the scenario is REQUIREMENT-GENERAL — merely on the broad theme of the parent requirement while asserting no clause of THIS specific criterion; an AC-level pointer claims criterion-specific coverage, and requirement-level relevance has its own weaker pointer shape, so anchor the verdict on assertion-to-clause MAPPING and NEVER on topical or lexical overlap between the scenario and the criterion. It is HOLLOW when the Then step is a MIRROR-TEXT tautology: a restatement of the criterion as a conclusion while the SCENARIO ITSELF contributes NO harness-evaluable element. semantic_findings.predicate: A Gherkin scenario legitimately COVERS an acceptance criterion when AT LEAST ONE of the scenario's OUTCOME assertions — a Then step and its And/But continuations — verifies AT LEAST ONE CLAUSE of THIS specific criterion's own required behavior. The unit of judgment is ONE (scenario, criterion) pair: decide only whether THIS scenario verifies THIS criterion — NEVER whether the criterion is fully or exhaustively covered, and never look for sibling scenarios the judge cannot see. A scenario is SOUND when even ONE Then-side assertion maps to even ONE clause of a multi-clause criterion: PARTIAL coverage of a multi-clause criterion is SOUND, because completeness is not the judged question and a narrow scenario is still genuine coverage. A scenario is SOUND when it verifies just ONE FACET of a criterion whose full coverage is split across several scenarios: verdicts are pair-local and monotone under decomposition, so a single-facet scenario must NOT be called hollow merely because other scenarios carry the remaining clauses. A scenario that EXERCISES the criterion's condition in its Given/When steps AND asserts a downstream consequence of that condition in a Then step is SOUND. The reference is HOLLOW (FAIL) when NO Then-side assertion maps to ANY clause of THIS criterion. It is HOLLOW when the citation is SETUP-ONLY: the criterion's condition appears ONLY as a Given step or background fixture — a precondition the scenario depends on — while every Then asserts a DIFFERENT target's behavior; exercising the criterion as setup is NOT verifying it. It is HOLLOW when the scenario's real subject is a SIBLING criterion: its assertions verify a DIFFERENT acceptance criterion (of the same or another requirement), not this one. It is HOLLOW when the scenario is REQUIREMENT-GENERAL — merely on the broad theme of the parent requirement while asserting no clause of THIS specific criterion; an AC-level pointer claims criterion-specific coverage, and requirement-level relevance has its own weaker pointer shape, so anchor the verdict on assertion-to-clause MAPPING and NEVER on topical or lexical overlap between the scenario and the criterion. An acceptance criterion states one or more independently testable clauses; a scenario COVERS the criterion by CHECKING, through an observable assertion, that one of those clauses holds. The unit of judgment is ONE (scenario, criterion) pair: decide only whether THIS scenario verifies THIS criterion — NEVER whether the criterion is fully or exhaustively covered, and never look for sibling scenarios the judge cannot see. A scenario is SOUND when even ONE Then-side assertion maps to even ONE clause of a multi-clause criterion: PARTIAL coverage of a multi-clause criterion is SOUND, because completeness is not the judged question and a narrow scenario is still genuine coverage. A scenario is SOUND when it verifies just ONE FACET of a criterion whose full coverage is split across several scenarios: verdicts are pair-local and monotone under decomposition, so a single-facet scenario must NOT be called hollow merely because other scenarios carry the remaining clauses. A scenario that EXERCISES the criterion's condition in its Given/When steps AND asserts a downstream consequence of that condition in a Then step is SOUND. The reference is HOLLOW (FAIL) when NO Then-side assertion maps to ANY clause of THIS criterion. It is HOLLOW when the citation is SETUP-ONLY: the criterion's condition appears ONLY as a Given step or background fixture — a precondition the scenario depends on — while every Then asserts a DIFFERENT target's behavior; exercising the criterion as setup is NOT verifying it. It is HOLLOW when the scenario's real subject is a SIBLING criterion: its assertions verify a DIFFERENT acceptance criterion (of the same or another requirement), not this one. It is HOLLOW when the scenario is REQUIREMENT-GENERAL — merely on the broad theme of the parent requirement while asserting no clause of THIS specific criterion; an AC-level pointer claims criterion-specific coverage, and requirement-level relevance has its own weaker pointer shape, so anchor the verdict on assertion-to-clause MAPPING and NEVER on topical or lexical overlap between the scenario and the criterion. It is HOLLOW when the Then step is a MIRROR-TEXT tautology: a restatement of the criterion as a conclusion while the SCENARIO ITSELF contributes NO harness-evaluable element. The scenario contributes an evaluable element when its own Given/When fixtures instantiate the criterion's condition or input, or its own Then states a checkable outcome, artifact, status or error code, enumerated constructs, displayed output, named schema, precedence, or branching beyond quoting the criterion — such a Then is SOUND even when its wording verbatim-copies the criterion's own sentence, AND even when that copy sits behind a framing preamble such as "the system behaves such that", "it holds that", "as specified", "per the criterion", "the result reflects that", or "the behavior is exactly that". A framing preamble is NEVER by itself a mirror-text signal: strip it and judge the underlying assertion. PURE-PARROT mirror-text (HOLLOW) is RESERVED for the narrow case where the scenario merely ASSUMES or PROJECTS the criterion's result BY CONSTRUCTION — its Given/When assert the criterion's own conclusion as a precondition rather than instantiating a condition to exercise — while the Then restates that conclusion as an ABSTRACT satisfaction claim naming no concrete, harness-checkable observable. A conclusion-form copy that names a concrete checkable observable, backed by Given/When that instantiate the condition, is SOUND; quoting evaluable words fails to demonstrate evaluable behavior ONLY when nothing in the scenario exercises or checks them. Lexical or topical overlap, and a restating preamble, are NEVER by themselves a mirror-text signal; the missing scenario-contributed evaluable check is. It is HOLLOW when the scenario is a STALE near-miss: it faithfully verifies the criterion's PREVIOUS text and no assertion maps to a clause of the criterion's CURRENT text — an almost-sound, drifted scenario is still hollow.
